words.sense: Absence of effective governing authority or enforceable order
misconceptions: Treating every crowded disorderly scene as lawlessness.
Assuming rules still work merely because a rulebook exists.

words.sense: Severe confusion and disorder despite possible authority
misconceptions: Treating every crowded disorderly scene as lawlessness.
Confusing a loss of authority with an ordinary logistical mess.

semantic_axes.description: Anarchy involves the lack or collapse of effective authority; chaos describes disorder even when authority still exists.

edges.boundary_rule: Anarchy involves the lack or collapse of effective authority; chaos describes disorder even when authority still exists.
clues_b: confusion while rules remain in force

chains.frame: Which word best describes what happens to Jamal's club?

beats.text: The club leader resigns, no replacement takes charge, and members stop accepting any rules for meetings.
beats.decisive_clue: no recognized authority to enforce club rules
beats.reason: The initial evidence is no recognized authority to enforce club rules; it best supports anarchy.

beats.text: They begin making conflicting decisions with nobody empowered to settle them.
beats.reason: The disputes follow from the absence of a recognized decision-maker.

chains.feedback_short: The disputes follow from the absence of a recognized decision-maker.
chains.feedback_deep: Anarchy means disorder caused by a power vacuum; chaos means confusion or disorder, whatever its cause. The disputes follow from the absence of a recognized decision-maker.
chains.contrast_rule: Anarchy has no effective authority; chaos has no clear order.

beats.text: The chef is wearing a new apron today.
beats.reason: The apron changes nothing; the chef still leads during the confusion.
